summary: DXT color encoder helper (__thiscall): converts float RGBA vertex data into packed 32-bit words with R, G and A each 8 bits (scales 128.0, 128.0 and 255.0); the B channel is not used. If the format-conversion flag this[1042] (byte 0x1048) is set, a4 is first replaced by the DirectXVertexBufferFormatConversion result. Computes a tile sample base at this[11] (byte 0x2C) offset by the (a2,a3) 4x4 block position, calls UtilityFunction_7473, then loops over this[1046] (byte 0x1058) vertices adding the tile sample to each scaled channel and writing one word per vertex (low byte R, next byte G, third byte A). Returns the conversion-state global dword_8B009C.

local_names.v4: result of DirectXVertexBufferFormatConversion, reassigned to a4
local_names.v5: output word pointer (advances per written vertex; uninitialized in the raw source)
local_names.v7: byte offset into the source vertex array (advances 16 per vertex)
local_names.v9: word whose low byte is G and high byte is A
local_names.v12: R channel scaled by 128.0 plus the tile sample
local_names.v13: G channel scaled by 128.0 plus the tile sample
local_names.v14: A channel scaled by 255.0 plus the tile sample
local_names.v15: tile sample base pointer at this+0x2C plus the encoded block offset

operations.description: Save the this pointer in v17 and initialize the vertex counter v6 to zero.
Guard on the format-conversion flag this[1042] (byte 0x1048); when non-zero the source vertex buffer is remapped before conversion.
Invoke DirectXVertexBufferFormatConversion(this, a4), restore this from v17, and replace a4 with the returned converted pointer.
Compute the tile sample base v15 = this[11] (byte 0x2C) + 4 * ((a3 & 3) + 8 * (a2 & 3)), encoding the 4x4 block position from the masked a2/a3 indices.
Call UtilityFunction_7473() unconditionally before the conversion loop.
Guard on the vertex count this[1046] (byte 0x1058); when zero the do-while body is skipped.
do-while loop over this[1046] (byte 0x1058) vertices, incrementing v6 and advancing the source offset v7 by 16 bytes per iteration.

Per vertex, read the tile sample v16 = float at v15 + 4*(v6 & 3) and form each scaled channel: v12 = float at a4+v7 * 128.0 + v16, v13 = float at a4+v7+4 * 128.0 + v16, v14 = float at a4+v7+12 * 255.0 + v16.

Pack the channels into a 32-bit word: low byte v8 = (int)v12, high byte of v9 = (int)v14, low byte of v9 = (int)v13, then write *v5++ = v8 | (v9 << 8); so R occupies the low byte, G the next byte, A the third byte.
Return the conversion-state global dword_8B009C as the function result.
